params.name: b
params.resample_while: lcm(a, b) == a or lcm(a, b) == b

params.name: r
params.resample_while: r == 0 or r == q or u * r + p == 0 or h * r + j <= 0

solution: The denominators are ${=a}$ and ${=b}$, so the common denominator is ${=d}$.
Multiply every term on both sides by ${=d}$: ${=d}\times\frac{{=u}x+{=p}}{{=a}}-{=d}\times\frac{x-{=q}}{{=b}}={=d}\times{=v}$
Remove the brackets. The minus sign in front of the second bracket changes both signs inside it: ${=m*u}x+{=m*p}-{=n}x+{=n*q}={=w}$

Check by substituting $x={=r}$ into the left-hand side: $\frac{{=u*r+p}}{{=a}}-\frac{{=r-q}}{{=b}}=\frac{{=m*(u*r+p)}}{{=d}}-\frac{{=n*(r-q)}}{{=d}}=\frac{{=w}}{{=d}}$, which equals the right-hand side ${=v}$.
notes: Advanced tier, generalises book ex4-1-24 ((x+2)/4 - (x-6)/3 = 1/2, answer 24): two binomial numerators, subtraction between them, and a fractional right-hand side. The book's own twist is the minus sign in front of the second bracket. Denominators come from {2,3,4,6} with neither dividing the other (so both multipliers m, n are at least 2); the first numerator carries x-coefficient u (2 or 3) and u is resampled so the collected coefficient h = u*m - n is at least 2 (no '1x' is ever printed). The answer r is drawn first and the right-hand side v = w/d computed from it, so v is a positive fraction or integer and every instance has a whole-number answer; r is kept away from 0, from q and from a zero first numerator. Hand-checked: a=4, b=3, u=2, p=1, q=2, r=5 gives (2x+1)/4 - (x-2)/3 = 7/4, 3(2x+1) - 4(x-2) = 21, 2x + 11 = 21, x = 5; a=3, b=2, u=3, p=4, q=5, r=-2 gives (3x+4)/3 - (x-5)/2 = 17/6, 2(3x+4) - 3(x-5) = 17, 3x + 23 = 17, 3x = -6, x = -2.
